'''''Star Wars Battlefront''''' is a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] from [[DICE]], a game developer owned by [[Electronic Arts]]. It is DICE's take on the format presented in the [[Star Wars Battlefront (series)|first two ''Battlefront'' games]], which were released in [[2004]] and [[2005]].

==Publisher's summary==
''Star Wars''™'' Battlefront''™'' ''is the ultimate'' Star Wars ''battle experience, brought to life by the creators of ''Battlefield''. Fight in epic ''Star Wars'' battles on iconic planets and rise through the ranks playing as the heroic Rebellion or the evil Galactic Empire''.<ref name="E3 2014">{{EASWYouTube|2yKv45X_OIo|Star Wars Battlefront | Official Trailer | E3 2014}}</ref>''

==Gameplay==
===Overview===
[[File:Heroes_and_Villains-SW_Battlefront.png|thumb|left|200px|The 14 playable "heroes"]]
Unlike previous ''Battlefront'' entries, this game does not have a story of its own. Instead, it reinterprets the [[Galactic Civil War|stories and battles]] presented in the [[original trilogy]],<ref name="Canon Complicated">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/04/29/star-wars-battlefront-canon-is-complicated|text=Star Wars: Battlefront Canon Is 'Complicated'|author=Dyer, Mitch|date=2015-04-29|archivedate=20150501022114}}</ref> alongside some battles presented in the novel ''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]'', such as the [[Siege of Inyusu Tor]]. The game has the option to switch at will between first-person mode and third-person mode, much like the previous entries in the series. Instead of a single-player campaign, the game features a set of co-op missions that can be played alone, online, or offline with split-screen. Players are able to play as hero and villain characters such as [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and [[Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Game" /> Each player is outfitted with a partner, and the duo are able to spawn on each other and share loadouts. DICE based the game's AI on the ''Star Wars'' films, but tweaked it to make it accessible.<ref name="OXM July">''Official Xbox Magazine'' July 2015 issue</ref> Classes are not featured in the game, for the player is able to freely customize their weapons, character, Star Cards and hands, and traits.<ref name="Gamespot Cautious Return">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/the-cautious-return-of-star-wars-battlefront/1100-6426701|text=The Cautious Return of Star Wars Battlefront|author=Watters, Chris|date=2015-04-18|archivedate=20150419031215}}</ref> When the game first installs on the system, players have the opportunity to play a mini-game as it is loading. They take the role of Darth Vader and face waves of Rebel troopers inside Echo Base (similar to the singleplayer Hero Battles).<ref name="Battlefront loading">''Star Wars Battlefront'' installation</ref>

===Multiplayer===
Unlike DICE's previous games, ''Battlefront'' does not use the Battlelog system to connect players. Rather, a new system was built from scratch,<ref name="Battlelog">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/star-wars-battlefront-won-t-use-battlefield-s-batt/1100-6426735|text=Star Wars: Battlefront Won't Use Battlefield's Battlelog System|date=2015-04-18|archivedate=20150420141903}}</ref> and is featured as an in-game menu.<ref name="Gamescom QA">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/gamescom-twitter-q-and-a|text=''Star Wars''™ Battlefront™ Gamescom Twitter Q&A;|date=2015-08-08}}</ref>

In January 2016, the game was updated to include new concepts such as private matches and timed Community Events for players to take an active role in. The update also included multiplayer balances.<ref name="The Road Ahead">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/star-wars-battlefront-the-road-ahead|text=''Star Wars'' Battlefront - The Road Ahead|author=Contereras, Batttlefront team|date=2016-01-26}}</ref>

The three largest game modes are ''Walker Assault'', ''Supremacy'', and ''Turning Point'', allowing 40 players (20 per team) to play in a single match. The other game modes will have smaller player counts. Other multiplayer modes included are ''Fighter Squadron'', ''Blast'', ''Drop Zone'', ''Cargo'', and ''Droid Run''.<ref name="Multiplayer">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/features/game-modes|text=Star Wars Battlefront Game Modes}}</ref>

''Blast'' is a standard Team Deathmatch, with 10 players on each side. Lead Level Designer Dennis Brännvall revealed that there would be a 10-minute/100-kill limit, and that the mode would not include a chance to play as a Hero or Villain.<ref name="Blast Mode">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/blast-mode-team-deathmatch-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Blast Mode: Team Deathmatch in a Galaxy Far, Far, Away…|date=2015-07-30}}</ref>

''Cargo'' is an interpretation of the classic Capture the Flag game mode. Each team controls a base with their own captured cargo. Teams need to run into the opposing teams' base, pick up their cargo and bring it back to their own base, while also defending their base from the opposing team. However, you do not need cargo in your own base in order to capture the opposing team's cargo, creating a "tug of war" experience.<ref name="Cargo">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/cargo-a-star-wars-battlefront-twist-on-a-classic-game-mode|text=Cargo: A Star Wars Battlefront Twist on a Classic Game Mode|date=2015-10-12}}</ref>

In ''Droid Run'', three [[GNK-series power droid]]s roam the map. In small maps with six players on each team, players must locate the droids, chase them and capture and defend them for their team.<ref name="Droid Run">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/go-on-a-droid-run-in-star-wars-battlefront|text=Go on a Droid Run in Star Wars Battlefront|date=2015-10-12}}</ref>

''Drop Zone'' is based on King of the Hill. Players need to control the landing sites of drop pods as they fall from the sky. The first team to capture five of these pods or the team who holds the majority of the drop pods after 10 minutes will emerge the victor.<ref name="King of the Hill">{{WebCite|url=http://www.polygon.com/2015/9/8/9282225/star-wars-battlefront-drop-zone-mode|text=Star Wars Battlefront's new mode is 'king of the hill' in a galaxy far, far away|author=McWhertor, Michael|date=2015-09-09|archivedate=20150911021159}}</ref>

''Fighter Squadron'' allows players to pilot the ships that appear in the game. In these matches, each team consists of 10 players, along with additional AI teammates. Alongside these, each team also has a transport or shuttle attempting to make it across the map safely. The opposing team attempts to shoot down this transport or shuttle before it can escape. Players are also to grab hero pickups that will allow them to play as the ''Millennium Falcon'', ''Slave I'', ''Red Five'', or Vader's TIE Advanced.<ref name="Gamescom QA" />

In ''Heroes vs Villains'', each team consists of 6 players. Three players spawn as the heroes of their corresponding team, while the other three spawn as troopers. However, if you are a hero/villain and you are defeated, you will spawn as a normal trooper. The objective is to take out the opposing teams' characters.<ref name="Heroes vs Villains">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/heroes-vs-villains-the-clash-of-iconic-star-wars-characters|text=Heroes vs Villains: The Clash of Iconic Star Wars Characters|date=2015-10-20}}</ref>

[[File:Tatooine_Fighter_Squadron-SW_Battlefront.png|thumb|left|300px|Fighter Squadron on Tatooine]]
''Hero Hunt'' pits one hero or villain, depending on the planet, against seven soldiers of the opposing team. The objective is to defeat that hero or villain; however, when this character is defeated, the player who defeated them will become the new hero or villain. The objective of the player who spawned as a hero or villain is to take out the seven soldiers of the opposing team and keep yourself alive.<ref name="Hero Hunt">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/hero-hunt-beat-or-become-the-legends-of-star-wars|text=Hero Hunt: Beat or Become the Legends of Star Wars™|date=2015-10-12}}</ref>

''Supremacy'', based on the classic Conquest mode, is a 10-minute match which features five control points for the teams to capture, with each side owning two at the start of the match. Each one will unlock in sequence as they are captured, and the maps will be the largest in the game.<ref name="Supremacy">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/supremacy-mode-all-out-galactic-conquest|text=Own the Battlefront in Supremacy Mode|date=2015-08-08}}</ref>

''Walker Assault'' is partially based on the classic Rush game mode. Imperial forces are attempting to push their AT-ATs to the end of the map in order to destroy either a [[GR-75 medium transport|Rebel transport]] or base. In three separate phases, Rebel forces must activate two uplinks in order to call in [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wing bombers]] to attack the Empire's AT-AT's and prevent them from reaching their destination. In order to prevent this, Imperial forces must keep these uplinks offline. The Imperials are the only faction allowed to use ground vehicles in this mode. Players on the Imperial side are allowed to use AT-ATs and AT-STs; AT-STs are a smaller, two-legged version of the AT-AT that have less health than the AT-AT. In this game mode, the AT-ATs are referred to as Imperial Walkers, while the AT-STs are referred to as Scout Transports. Players can use the scout transports until they are destroyed, while AT-AT pilots only have a certain amount of time. This time can be extended by getting kills in the walker. The orbital strike ability can be used while inside the Imperial Walker to clear the area of Rebel ground forces.

''Turning Point'', introduced in the free ''Battle of Jakku'' DLC, is a large game mode allowing up to 40 players total. In this game mode, Imperial forces command three control points that Rebel forces are attempting to capture. On the outskirts of the map, the Empire controls a large base, which is the main target for Rebel forces.<ref name="jakkublogpost">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/get-a-first-glimpse-of-the-battle-of-jakku-in-star-wars-battlefront|text=Get a First Glimpse of the Battle of Jakku in Star Wars Battlefront}}</ref>

Extraction, in the ''Outer Rim DLC'', is another multiplayer mode. Rebel forces have entered the Outer Rim to extract a shipment. They must return to the transport before the time runs out or the Empire stops them.<ref name="Outer Rim post">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/outer-rim|text=Star Wars Battlefront - Outer Rim|nobackup=1}}</ref>

Sabotage, in the ''Bespin'' DLC, is a multiplayer mode which takes place in two parts. The Empire are using Tibanna Gas Generators to power their tractor beams, preventing Rebel transports from escaping Cloud City. The Rebels must blow up the generators, and if successful, must defend their extraction point. The Empire must stop the Rebels and hunt them down.<ref name="Bespin DLC">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/bespin-welcome-to-cloud-city|text=Bespin – Welcome To Cloud City|date=2016-06-21|nolive=1}}</ref>

Battle Station, in the ''Death Star'' DLC, is a three-phase multiplayer game mode where it starts out in space with the Rebels trying to take out a Star Destroyer, then moving inside the station to extract a droid, and finally recreating the Battle of Yavin, adding Red 5 and Darth Vader's TIE Fighter.<ref name="Gamescon Death Star">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/news-from-gamescom|text=''Star Wars'' Battlefront: Death Star New Mode Details|date=2016-08-17}}</ref>

===Single-player and co-op===
[[File:Tatooine_Survival-SW_Battlefront.png|thumb|right|300px|A single-player game of Survival on Tatooine]]
Single-player and co-op are available in the form of a series of game modes collectively known as Missions. These "missions" include Survival, Battles, Hero Battles and Trials.<ref name="Singleplayer">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/features/missions|text=Gameplay Missions}}</ref> Survival will only offer the chance to play as Rebels, although players can join either side in other modes.<ref name="Community Update 2">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/star-wars-battlefront-community-update-2|text=''Star Wars™ Battlefront™'' Community Update #2|author=Everett, Matthew|date=2015-07-28}}</ref>

In the Survival mission, you (and your partner, should you have one) must hold off against 15 waves of Imperial forces. Each wave gets increasingly more difficult than the last. Throughout the mission, several drop pods will descend to the ground, allowing you to capture them for power-ups. You can only play as a Rebel trooper in this Mission.<ref name="2015 Deep Dive">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/survival-mission-e3-2015-deep-dive|text=''Star Wars''™ Battlefront™ Missions: Take on the Empire Solo or Co-Op with a Friend in Survival|date=2015-06-16|nolive=1}}</ref>

Training consists of five varied Missions to familiarize players with the gameplay and its mechanics. The player can play as either Rebel troopers or Imperial Stormtroopers, depending on the Mission. In the tutorial Probe Droid, players can learn of the various Star Cards, which make up their loadout, weapons, and "blowing up Imperial hardware." In the Beggar's Cannon mission, players will be able to pilot X-wings in the skies of Tatooine while combating enemy TIE fighters. The mission called Invasion is relatively similar, although players this time pilot Snowspeeders on Hoth. In Overpower, the player acts as an Imperial soldier piloting an AT-ST. In the Endor Chase mission, the player must chase Rebel troopers who have hijacked speeder bikes. Finally, in the Mission called The Dark Side, the player can play as Darth Vader while attacking a Rebel base on Hoth. Should you play with a partner, they will be assigned to playing as Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="Learn the Ways">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/training-missions-learn-the-ways-of-star-wars-battlefront|text=Training Missions: Learn the Ways of Star Wars Battlefront|date=2015-10-20}}</ref>

Battles pits the player against enemy AI in a deathmatch-like scenario. Playing with a partner allows one to play against them as well, either backed by enemy AI or in one-versus-one action. The goal of the player is to reach 100 points; however, in order for a point to count by taking out an enemy, the player must pick up a token they drop when taken down, otherwise the kill will not count. Hero Battles plays the same way, except it allows the player to control a hero or villain rather than playing as a regular soldier.<ref name="Battles and Hero Battles">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/battles-and-hero-battles-online-or-split-screen-1-vs-1-action|text=Battles and Hero Battles: Online or Split-Screen 1 vs 1 Action|date=2015-10-20}}</ref> At most, your team can have 5 AI allies while the opposing team can have 14 enemy AI.<ref name="Answers">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/forums/discussion/5809/answers-to-your-questions|text=Answers To Your Questions|date=2015-10-30}}</ref>

Skirmish was introduced on [[July 21]], 2016. Based off of the classic instant action game mode from the original [[Star Wars Battlefront (series)|''Star Wars: Battlefront'']] games, Skirmish allows the player to play the online multiplayer game modes Walker Assault and Fighter Squadron offline against AI.<ref name="Skirmish">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/whats-next-for-star-wars-battlefront-this-summer|text=What's Next For Star Wars Battlefront This Summer|author=Brannvall, Dennis|date=2016-07-12}}</ref>

==Development==
[[File:Finse_Norway-SW_Battlefront.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The DICE team visited [[Wikipedia:Finse|Finse]], [[Wikipedia:Norway|Norway]], the original filming location of [[Hoth]].]]
EA first unveiled their plans for the game at the [[Wikipedia:Electronic Entertainment Expo|Electronic Entertainment Expo (E3)]] on [[June 10]], [[2013]].<ref name="Forbes" /> In the hopes of creating a realistic, immersive experience for players, the DICE team visited the [[Lucasfilm Archives]] as well as filming locations for the films.<ref name="E3 2014" /> The images were then turned into the 3D format by the process of photogrammetry.<ref name="Photogrammetry">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/how-we-used-photogrammetry|text=How we used Photogrammetry to Capture Every Last Detail for ''Star Wars™ Battlefront™''|date=2015-05-21}}</ref> Additionally, preparing for the sound design, the DICE team worked with Lucasfilm and had access to their ''Star Wars'' sound library. They also had the chance to work with sound designers [[Ben Burtt]] and [[Matthew Wood]]. Audio Director Ben Minto and his team also recorded sounds in a Foley session with Dennie Thorpe and Jana Vance, and on location.<ref name="Sound design">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/creating-the-sounds-of-star-wars-battlefront|text=Creating the Sounds of Star Wars™ Battlefront™}}</ref> On December 4, 2013, EA announced that projects from DICE, including ''Star Wars: Battlefront'', would be delayed until performance issues in their video game ''[https://battlefield.fandom.com/wiki/Battlefield_4 Battlefield 4]'' were fixed.<ref name="Delay">{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/12/04/battlefield-4-problems-halt-future-projects-and-expansions|text=Battlefield 4 Problems Halt 'Future Projects' and Expansions|author=Dyer, Mitch|date=2013-12-04|archivedate=20131205021218}}</ref> A subsequent announcement from EA clarified that the patch work would not affect upcoming release dates.<ref name="Not delayed">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/wall-street-taking-notice-of-battlefield-4-issues-as-ea-stock-falls/1100-6416566|text=Wall Street taking notice of Battlefield 4 issues as EA stock falls|author=Makuch, Eddie|date=2013-12-05|archivedate=20131206060705}}</ref> Executive producer Patrick Bach revealed that the team is trying to create a new experience for players, one that is not directly inspired by DICE's ''Battlefield'' series while still keeping ties to the original ''Star Wars: Battlefront'' series, such as perspective switch.<ref name="OXM July" />

Senior Producer [[Sigurlina Ingvarsdottir]] revealed in an interview that DICE originally asked to make the game due to the studio being fans of ''Star Wars'' and having experience on previous multiplayer experiences such as ''Battlefield''. They wanted to create a game that would allow fans to immerse themselves in ''Star Wars'' fantasies and be able to play in their own way, such as driving an Imperial vehicle or having Luke Skywalker face Boba Fett. As part of the process, they visited the Lucasfilm archives.<ref name="Producer E3 interview">{{YouTube|video=mqbzGocossI|text=Stage Demo: Star Wars: Battlefront - E3 2015|channel=channel/UCbu2SsF-Or3Rsn3NxqODImw|name=GameSpot}}</ref>

The game does not feature elements from the [[prequel trilogy]] due to not wishing to "violate canon."<ref name="Polygon OT">{{WebCite|url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/1/29/10871438/star-wars-battlefront-ea-canon|text=Here's why Star Wars Battlefront content is sticking with the original trilogy|author=Frank, Allegra|date=2016-01-05|archivedate=20160129204549}}</ref>

A campaign was originally planned for the game, but was cut in order for the game to release in time for [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']].<ref name="Campaign Cut">{{WebCite|url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/167478-Star-Wars-Battlefront-no-Campaign-Because-of-The-Force-Awakens|text=Battlefront's Campaign Was Cut so it Could Launch With Episode VII|author=Bogos, Steven|date=2016-05-18|archivedate=20181117153111}}</ref>

The game became playable via EA Access in December, 2016.<ref name="EA Access">{{WebCite|url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/12/7/13867314/battlefront-ea-access-vault|text=Star Wars Battlefront will be added to EA Access next week|author=Good, Owen S.|date=2016-12-07|archivedate=20161207175545}}</ref>

===Music===
{{Main|Star Wars Battlefront (soundtrack)}}
[[Gordy Haab]] composed and orchestrated the [[Star Wars Battlefront (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] of the game. The music was performed by the [[London Symphony Orchestra]] and [[London Voices]] and was recorded at [[Abbey Road Studios]]<ref name="Main Theme" /> [[John Williams]]' music of the [[Star Wars saga|''Star Wars'' saga]] was also used for the game.

==Release and reception==
[[File:Glimpse_of_Star_Wars_Battlefront-Celebration_Anaheim.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The inside of the ''[[Home One]]''–inspired ''Star Wars Battlefront'' booth at Celebration Anaheim]]
On [[March 19]], [[2015]], EA announced that the game would make its debut at [[Celebration Anaheim (2015)|Celebration Anaheim]] in April 2015. In announcing the debut, EA stated that they "could not think of a better or more appropriate place to debut the game officially for the first time than the premier event that celebrates the ''Star Wars'' universe and the legions of fans who have fallen in love with it."<ref name="Celebration Debut">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=news/battlefront-to-debut-at-celebration|text=''Star Wars''™ Battlefront™ to Debut at ''Star Wars''™ Celebration|date=2015-03-19}}</ref> Soon after, EA released a letter to fans saying the first gameplay footage would be seen at E3 2015.<ref name="Gameplay footage 1">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/dear-galaxy|text="Dear Galaxy"|author=Fegraeus, Niklas|date=2015-05-14}}</ref>

Gameplay footage was first shown at the Electronic Entertainment Expo 2015,<ref name="Gameplay footage 1" /> where the game garnered multiple award nominations from attendees, and received 39 wins.<ref name="E3 awards">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/star-wars-battlefront-e3-awards|text=''Star Wars™ Battlefront™'' E3 Awards|date=2015-06-25}}</ref>

Beta testing was originally open from [[October 8]] through [[October 12]], during which players were able to access three game modes: Walker Assault (Hoth), Drop Zone (Sullust), and Survival Mission (Tatooine).<ref name="Armed and Operational Updated">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-battlefront-beta-armed-and-operational|text=''Star Wars Battlefront'' Beta: Armed and Operational - UPDATED!}}</ref> On October 12, the Beta was extended one day to [[October 13]].<ref name="betapass">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/extending-the-beta-and-the-announcement-of-the-star-wars-battlefront-season-pass-and-ultimate-edition|text=Extending the Beta and the Announcement of the ''Star Wars'' Battlefront Season Pass and Ultimate Edition.|date=2015-10-12}}</ref> Reportedly, the beta drew nine million participants.<ref name="Galaxy Wire Oct 13">{{SW|url=news/galaxy-wire-star-wars-news-from-around-the-web-october-13-2015|text=Galaxy Wire: ''Star Wars'' News from Around the Web - October 13, 2015}}</ref>

*Standard edition<ref name="Buy">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/buy|text=Pre-Order Star Wars™ Battlefront|nolive=1}}</ref>
*Deluxe edition (includes digital exclusives)<ref name="Buy" />
*Darth Vader-themed PlayStation 4 bundle;<ref name="Vader PS4 Bundle">{{SW|url=news/disney-announces-darth-vader-inspired-playstation-4-bundles-at-d23|text=Disney Announces Darth Vader-Inspired Playstation 4 Bundles at D23|nolive=1}}</ref> Lucasfilm and Sony gave away some of these in a Twitter sweepstakes.<ref name="PS4 sweepstakes">{{SW|url=news/limited-edition-darth-vader-playstation-4-sweepstakes|text=Limited Edition Darth Vader PlayStation 4 Sweepstakes!}}</ref>

[[Wikipedia:Wal Mart|Wal Mart]] sold an exclusive bundle that included the Deluxe Edition of the game and a mini-refrigerator modeled after [[Han Solo]] in [[carbonite]].<ref name="Han Solo Mini Fridge">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/this-130-star-wars-battlefront-bundle-comes-with-h/1100-6430598|text=This $130 Star Wars Battlefront Bundle Comes With Han Solo Mini-Fridge|author=Makuch, Eddie|date=2015-09-15|archivedate=20150917132751}}</ref>

===Downloadable content===
[[File:DLC_Packs-SW_Battlefront.png|thumb|left|300px|''Star Wars Battlefront''{{'s}} four expansion packs]]
A ''Battlefront'' companion app was released by the Apple App Store and Google Play. It includes the mini-game "Base Command," which can be used to earn credits that can unlock content in ''Battlefront''. The app was first made available during the October 2015 beta test.<ref name="Play Base Command">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/connect-with-friends-with-star-wars-battlefront-companion|text=Play Base Command and Connect with Friends with the ''Star Wars'' Battlefront Companion|date=2015-10-01}}</ref>

On October 12, 2015, EA announced that the game would have four expansion packs, and that a $50 Season Pass would be available that would cover all expansions and grant the purchaser early access to each.<ref name="betapass" />

On [[January 26]], [[2016]], EA revealed its planned free expansions and paid DLC packs.<ref name="The Road Ahead" />

====Star Wars Battlefront: Battle of Jakku====
On April 17, 2015, EA announced the first downloadable content for ''Star Wars Battlefront'', titled ''Star Wars Battlefront: [[Battle of Jakku]]''. It was released at no additional charge on December 8, 2015, approximately one week prior to the worldwide release of ''The Force Awakens''. Players who had pre-ordered ''Battlefront'' were eligible to play the downloadable content beginning on December 1, 2015, one week before those who had not pre-ordered.<ref name="Battle of Jakku Free DLC" />

====Star Wars Battlefront: Outer Rim====
This expansion pack was released on [[March 22]], 2016 for Season Pass holders.<ref name="Outer Rim DLC" /> Players now have the opportunity to play in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba's]] Palace and the factories of Sullust. The mode also introduces a new "Extraction" game mode, new star cards and weapons, and two new heroes and villains: [[Nien Nunb]] and [[Greedo]].<ref name="The Road Ahead" /> With the release of the pack, players now have access to Hutt Contracts: by completing challenges, they can unlock the new equipment.<ref name="Outer Rim DLC" />

====Star Wars Battlefront: Bespin====
This expansion pack was released on [[June 21]], 2016. It features five new maps set on and around the [[Cloud City]] of [[Bespin]] which support various modes.<ref name="The Road Ahead" /> It also includes new Star Cards, and a new type of multiplayer mode called Sabotage. The DLC also allowed players to take control of the Heroes [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Dengar]].<ref name="Coming Soon Spring">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/coming-soon-to-star-wars-battlefront-this-spring|text=Coming Soon to ''Star Wars'' Battlefront This Spring|date=2016-04-14}}</ref>

====Star Wars Battlefront: Death Star====
This expansion pack features the debut of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] and was released on September 20, 2016 for Season Pass holders.<ref name="The Road Ahead" /><ref name="LEVENTS">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/live-events|text=Live Events Calendar}}</ref> A teaser was released on July 16, showcasing vehicular gameplay above and around the Death Star, as well as multiple [[capital ship]]s. It was further confirmed that [[Chewbacca]] and [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] would serve as the heroes for the expansion pack.<ref name="SWC16">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/news-from-star-wars-celebration-europe|text=News from Star Wars™ Celebration Europe|date=2016-07-16}}</ref>

====Star Wars Battlefront: Rogue One: Scarif====
This expansion pack features maps set on [[Scarif]], a tropical [[planet]] that appears in the [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. The heroes for this DLC are [[Jyn Erso]] and [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]]. It was released on December 6, 2016 for holders of the Season Pass.<ref name="GamesRadar">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/star-wars-battlefronts-rogue-one-scarif-dlc-comes-out-december-6-take-your-first-look|text=Star Wars Battlefront's Rogue One: Scarif DLC comes out December 6, take your first look|author=Sheridan, Connor|date=2016-11-17|archivedate=20161118140107}}</ref>

====Star Wars Battlefront: Rogue One: X-wing VR Mission====
This free add-on adds a virtual reality mission to the game. It is exclusive to Playstation VR and was released around Christmas time, 2016. The experience was developed by DICE and [[Criterion Games]],<ref name="X-Wing VR announcement">{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/x-wing-vr-mission-announce|text=Star Wars™ Battlefront: X-Wing VR Mission on Target for Release Date this Holiday|nolive=1}}</ref> who previously worked on the Endor Chase mission,<ref name="IGN Galactic Racer">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/the-big-star-wars-galactic-racer-interview-why-its-not-open-world-how-its-story-mode-works-and-when-its-set|text=The Big Star Wars: Galactic Racer Interview — Why It's Not Open World, How Its Story Mode Works, and When It's Set|author=Tom Phillips|date=2026-02-17|archivedate=20260217144118|work=''[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]''}}</ref> and was announced at E3 2016.<ref name="X-Wing VR announcement" /> The team at Criterion Studios were able to integrate the game with ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' after working with [[Lucasfilm]].<ref name="Under the Hood">{{EA|url=play2016/news/under-the-hood-starwars-battlefront-vr-us|text=Under The Hood: Star Wars Battlefront Rogue One: X-wing VR|nolive=1}}</ref>
